T: Two cops. One case. Several misunderstandings.
D: A Hong Kong inspector and a loudmouth LA cop team up to find a kidnapped girl.
P: Serve the mains when Lee walks into the Foo Chow restaurant.
S: Foo Chow prawn and bamboo dumplings

Plump prawn dumplings with bamboo shoot, ginger and sesame, folded into wonton wrappers, steamed and served with chilli oil and black vinegar soy. Finely chop 400g peeled green prawns with 60g bamboo shoots, 1 tsp grated ginger, 2 sliced spring onions, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp cornflour and a pinch of salt. Place a teaspoon in the centre of each of 24 wonton wrappers, wet the edges and pleat closed. Steam on baking paper in a bamboo steamer for 7 minutes. Mix 3 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp black vinegar and 1 tbsp chilli oil for dipping.
Cabbage, carrot, shiitake and glass noodles stir-fried, cooled, rolled in spring roll pastry, fried at 180C. Sweet chilli.
Wings baked at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp, tossed in hot sauce and butter, ranch dip.
M: the Chinatown restaurant where it all kicks off
Beef chow fun: wide rice noodles wok-fried hot with marinated beef, bean sprouts, spring onion, dark and light soy.
Carter's fried chicken and mac plate
fried chicken and greens, Carter's order

Buttermilk fried chicken with a crunchy spiced crust, smoky braised greens with ham hock and a bubbling baked mac and cheese. Soak 1kg chicken pieces overnight in 500ml buttermilk with hot sauce and salt. Simmer 1 smoked ham hock in 1.5 litres water for 1 hour, add 2 bunches shredded kale or silverbeet and 2 tbsp vinegar and braise 30 minutes. Toss chicken in 250g flour with paprika, garlic powder and pepper, fry at 165C for 14 minutes. Cook 300g macaroni, stir into a sauce of 40g butter, 40g flour, 600ml milk and 200g cheddar, top with more cheese and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.
W: crack them open over the case
Thin vanilla batter in circles, baked at 180C for 6 minutes, folded around paper fortunes while hot.
K: Vodka shaken with chilled jasmine tea, lychee syrup and a squeeze of lime, strained into coupes with a whole lychee dropped in. Brew 1 jasmine tea bag in 120ml hot water for 3 minutes and cool. Drain a 565g tin of lychees, keeping the syrup. Shake 160ml vodka, the tea, 80ml lychee syrup and the juice of 1 lime with ice for 15 seconds. Strain into 4 chilled coupes and drop a lychee into each.

s.note: Crisp pastry rolls with cabbage, carrot, shiitake and glass noodles.
s.how: Soak 30g glass noodles in hot water for 5 minutes, drain and cut short. Stir-fry 120g shredded cabbage, 1 grated carrot and 60g finely sliced shiitake in 1 tsp oil for 4 minutes. Add the noodles and 1 tsp light soy sauce, stir 1 minute and cool completely. Divide among 8 spring roll pastry sheets, roll tightly and seal with a paste of 1 tsp flour and 1 tsp water. Fry in neutral oil at 180°C for 3 to 4 minutes until golden. Serve with 40ml sweet chilli sauce.

s.note: Crisp baked wings in hot butter sauce with cooling ranch dip.
s.how: Pat 600g chicken wings dry and season with 1/2 tsp salt. Bake on a rack at 220°C conventional for 45 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp and at least 74°C inside. Melt 25g butter and mix with 35ml hot sauce; toss through the wings. For a cooling ranch dip, mix 80g sour cream, 20g mayonnaise, 1 tbsp chopped chives, 1/4 tsp garlic powder and 1 tsp lemon juice. Serve beside the wings.

m.note: Wide rice noodles wok fried with beef, sprouts and spring onion.
m.how: Thinly slice 400g beef rump and marinate for 20 minutes with 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp cornflour and 1 tsp sesame oil. Separate 600g fresh wide rice noodles gently. Heat 1 tbsp neutral oil in a wok over high heat; stir-fry the beef in two batches for 2 minutes and set aside. Add another 1 tbsp oil and fry the noodles for 2 minutes. Add 150g bean sprouts, 3 sliced spring onions, 1 tbsp dark soy sauce and 1 tbsp light soy sauce. Return the beef and toss over high heat for 2 minutes until piping hot. Serve immediately.

w.note: Thin vanilla cookies folded around paper fortunes while still hot.
w.how: Write 8 fortunes on small clean food-safe paper strips. Whisk 2 egg whites with 50g caster sugar until foamy. Stir in 25g melted butter, 40g plain flour, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract and 1 tbsp water. Spread two thin 10cm circles at a time on a lined tray. Bake at 180°C conventional for 6 minutes until the edges turn golden. Working quickly while hot, place a fortune in each, fold in half and bend over a mug rim into the classic shape. Cool in muffin-tin cups. Repeat for 8 cookies. Remind everyone to remove the paper before eating.

d.how: Brew 1 jasmine tea bag in 120ml hot water for 3 minutes and cool. Drain a 565g tin of lychees, keeping the syrup. Shake 160ml vodka, the tea, 80ml lychee syrup and the juice of 1 lime with ice for 15 seconds. Strain into 4 chilled coupes and drop a lychee into each.
